evidence: eval: {enterOnCancel:'YES'}; js/core/ui.js:291-292 (function onKey(e){ if (e.key==='Enter' && !opts.danger) close(true); } on document); 51 ui.confirm call sites, the non-danger ones listed by grep in js/modules/focus.js, notifications.js, code.js, cardstats.js, governor-ui.js:450, jarun.js, medview.js, pwa.js:53

detail: The bell popover's first focusable is the '✓ Mark all as read' link, and the shared menu focuses the first control on open. Keyboard: Tab to the bell, Enter (open), Enter again = 42 notices marked read (synced), the popover closes, and nothing offers Undo. Reading state drives other surfaces (Home's report card stays 'New' until its notification is read, invariant 102c), so this also silently retires the 'New' report. The page version (#/notifications) has the same unguarded button.

title: First run writes four fake 'SAMPLE — … (edit me)' events into the real calendar; the mock exam becomes a real assessment that drives Home, alerts and the bell
evidence: shots/shell/empty-first-iphone.png, shots/shell/empty-home-mac.png; eval on reset account: assess ['SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)'], notify ['Afternoon review','SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)','23 plan topics carried over into this week'], toast text; js/modules/calendar.js:698-712; js/main.js:102
rootCause: A pre-hub demo seed still writes real records, and later domains (Exams migration, notifications, Google sync) treat them as the user's own.
fix: Drop seedSamples (the Sample data mode covers demos) or mark seeded rows {sample:true} so the exam migration, alerts, notify, Home ladder and ext sync skip them, with one 'Remove the examples' action. Add a short first-run card on Home (connect cloud, pick subjects, import Collection) instead.
detail: On an empty account main.js calls KOS.calendar.seedSamples(), which addEvent()s a SAMPLE mock exam (alerts 7 days and 1 day), a coursework deadline, a study block and a weekly maths lesson. The mock is then migrated into the Exams hub as a real assessment (state.exams.assessments = ['SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)']), so on day one Home's Focus card says 'Revise for SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)', the daily goal reads 'Revise for: SAMPLE…', a toast and a bell notice fire ('⏰ SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me) — 5 days away'), Upcoming lists both, and with Google Calendar connected they would be pushed two-way to the user's primary calendar. They are ordinary records: nothing marks them as samples or removes them, and the weekly lesson recurs forever. There is also no first-run welcome: the bell's other first notices are 'Afternoon review' and '23 plan topics carried over into this week' (the plan seed), and the Week's plan says '23 behind' on the first open. The app already has a proper separate Sample mode (KOS.dataMode 'sample').

title: Toast 'Undo' is unreachable without a pointer: the button is tabindex=-1 inside the aria-hidden #toast, and the spoken message never says Undo exists
devices: MacBook, iPad with keyboard, VoiceOver everywhere
evidence: eval: {ariaHidden:'true', tabindex:'-1', hitIsBtn:true}; js/core/ui.js:73-87; 6 call sites with {label:'Undo'}
rootCause: The toast was made aria-hidden for the live-region split (Phase F) before toasts gained actions.
fix: Give action toasts their own non-hidden container (role=status) with a focusable button; announce 'msg. Undo available, press ⌘Z' and bind ⌘Z/Ctrl+Z (outside text fields) to the most recent toast action while it is shown; pause the timer while hovered/focused.
detail: KOS.ui.toast(msg, bad, {label:'Undo', run}) appends the action button with tabindex '-1' into #toast, which carries aria-hidden='true'; the live region announces only msg. So keyboard users (Mac, iPad keyboard) cannot reach Undo, VoiceOver users never learn it exists, and there is no global ⌘Z outside the ink engine. The action toasts are the only Undo for: Home's plan tick (hub.js:964), Reminders' plan tick (reminders.js:344), the Daily Review's triage Tomorrow/Done/study block (dayreview.js:534,615,621,622). It also disappears after 8 s regardless of focus/hover (WCAG 2.2.1 timing).

title: Search ranks specification hits in syllabus order, not by relevance: 'binary' shows 'Fields, records and files' first and cuts 'Unsigned binary', 'Two's complement' and Code's 'Binary search trees' past the six shown
evidence: eval: search('binary') title hits at indexes [1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15] of 30; listbox options for 'binary','integration','dijkstra' (printed); js/core/search.js:31 (PER_DOMAIN 6), :42-49 (rank), :60-73 (specDomain: res.slice(0, PER_DOMAIN), no rank); js/modules/hub.js searchSpec (returns specHits in index order)
rootCause: Spec search is a filter, not a ranker, and the cross-domain layer truncates before ranking.
fix: Score spec hits: exact title > title word-start > title contains > spec text > flashcard, then subject order; rank before slicing; add a final 'See all N results' option that opens a results page (or expands the domain).
detail: The Specification domain takes KOS.hub.search's first six results without ranking: the hits come in SEARCH_INDEX order (CS 4.1… then Maths then Code), and search.js's rank() (title-starts-with first) is applied to every other domain but not to spec. For 'binary' 30 leaves match; title matches sit at positions 1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15 so 'Unsigned binary and binary arithmetic' (7), 'Signed binary using two's complement' (8) and all of Code's never appear, while 'Fields, records and files' (body text 'binary file') is first. 'integration' lists 'Partial fractions' above 'Integration as limit of a sum'; 'dijkstra' lists 'Kinds of abstraction' and 'Reverse Polish notation' (flashcard matches). There is no 'show all results' row, so a result past six cannot be reached.

title: Tapping a notification often lands on a generic page: Daily Review notices open Routines (not the review), routine-window notices ignore the routine, goal notices open the Goals list, and cold-start pushes drop object args
evidence: shots/shell/notify-review-open.png; eval: notify kinds review:routines:object, goal:goals:null; goal open -> '#/goals'; js/core/notify.js:196-199; js/core/dayreview.js:713; js/core/routines.js:560; js/modules/routines.js:469-473; js/core/goals.js:807; sw.js:147,154
rootCause: Producers set view/arg shapes the target views never learned to read, and the SW re-implements routing.
fix: Routines view: if arg.review open KOS.reviewSheet for that slot; if arg.routine open the player/editor. Goals notices: link {view:'goals', arg:{id}}. In the push payload send the router hash (KOS.router.routeFor) and let sw.js open it verbatim; for in-app kos-open keep view+arg.
detail: KOS.notify.open(item) does KOS.show(item.view, item.arg). Daily Review items carry {view:'routines', arg:{review:'afternoon'}} and routine windows {arg:{routine:id}}, but KOS.views.routines only reads arg.edit or a tab string, so both open Routines › Today and the review sheet never opens (verified: shots/shell/notify-review-open.png, no review dialog). Goal notices ('Goal reached — Goal 5') are pushed with {view:'goals', arg:null} and open the list (#/goals) instead of #/goals/<id>. The service worker builds its own cold-start hash ('#/'+view+'/'+arg, objects dropped, sw.js:147) instead of the router's routeFor, so a closed-app push for a review, a topic or a report week opens the section landing. One connected OS should take a notice straight to its record.

title: Kurenai cannot open 13 current pages: app_navigate's view list stops before Money, Reports, Routines, Files, Achievements, Connections, Storage, Pen and ink, the Assistant and the four study spaces (Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives)
evidence: eval: Object.keys(KOS.views) minus NAV_VIEWS = [pen, code, japanese, creatives, mind, routines, files, storage, connections, assistant, money, reports, achievements]; js/core/aitools.js:2735-2740 (NAV_VIEWS), :30 (SUBJECTS), :2741-2766 (app_navigate)

title: No first run: a new device opens straight onto a busy Home that is already "23 behind" with 3 unread notices, and nothing offers to sign in and bring the account's data over
devices: all (a new device or a fresh Home Screen install)
evidence: shots/shell/empty-home-mac.png, shots/shell/empty-first-iphone.png, shots/shell/empty-home-ipad.png; eval after reset: notify items [cal:1:2026-11-10:10080 SAMPLE — Mock exam, pace:carry:2026-11-02 23 plan topics carried over, review:evening:2026-11-05], #sync-status hidden; grep: no onboarding/firstRun code in js/; js/modules/calendar.js:704-708 (sample events); js/main.js:106 (KOS.pacing.ensureSeeded seeds the whole plan, past weeks included)
rootCause: Boot seeds sample events and the full plan unconditionally and has no pristine-state branch.
fix: Add a one-screen first run (shown while the state is pristine and signed out): "Sign in to bring your data" (cloud), "Start fresh", and the theme choice; suppress the sample calendar events and the pacing carry-over notice until the user chooses; show a quiet "Not synced — sign in" header chip while signed out on a device that has never synced.
detail: After a reset (a new iPad/iPhone, a cleared Safari, or the Home Screen app installed fresh) the app boots to Home with: the bell showing 3 unread ("SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)" alert, "23 plan topics carried over into this week", "Evening review"), Week's plan "23 behind", Upcoming listing a NEA milestone and two SAMPLE items, a Daily goal "Revise for: SAMPLE — Mock exam" and the review chip. There is no welcome, no step that explains what the app is, and no prompt to sign in to cloud sync, which is the only way the user's real data reaches the new device; the sign-in lives on Archive (#/data) with no link from Home, the bell or the empty states (the sync chip is hidden while signed out). A first open therefore shows alarming but fake state and buries the action that matters.

title: One toast slot: each new toast replaces the last, so in the Daily Review (or Home's Today ticks) only the most recent triage can be undone; toasts also vanish after a fixed 2.6 s whatever their length
evidence: js/core/ui.js:71-87 (single node, textContent replace, fixed 2600/8000 ms); Undo toasts at js/modules/dayreview.js:534, :615, :621, :622; js/modules/hub.js:964; js/modules/reminders.js:344
rootCause: The toast is a single-slot primitive and Undo was layered on it without a queue.
fix: Queue or stack toasts (at most 3, newest on top) and never drop one that carries an action until its time ends; scale duration to text length (e.g. 2.6 s + 60 ms/char, max 10 s) and pause on hover/focus; in the Daily Review keep an inline "Undo" on each triaged row instead of relying on the toast.
detail: KOS.ui.toast writes into the single #toast node (t.textContent = msg) and restarts one timer. The Daily Review's triage buttons (Tomorrow, ✓ Done, Study block, the step actions) each show "<title> · marked done — Undo"; triaging three items in a row leaves only the third's Undo — the first two are committed with no way back, although invariant 144 promises Undo for every change a review makes. Same on Home's Today ticks and Reminders' plan ticks. Any unrelated toast in the 8 s window (a save, a Focus message, the achievements count) also wipes a pending Undo. Plain toasts last 2.6 s regardless of length: "You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Wall." or an error with its reason cannot be read in that time (and the toast cannot be paused by hover or focus).

title: The URL does not record many pages: the Wall's tabs and set pages, an opened assignment or reminder, a review run all collapse to the bare route, so a reload, a bookmark or the Home Screen app relaunch lands on the wrong page
devices: all (worst in the installed iPad/iPhone app, which iOS relaunches)
evidence: eval: #/achievements/recent and #/achievements/titles render with the Sets tab selected; cold load of #/achievements/sets -> hash #/achievements; shots/shell/ach-titles-deeplink-mac.png (hash #/achievements/titles, Sets selected); js/core/router.js:30-148 (ENCODE/DECODE lack achievements, assignments, reminders, review, cardstats), :150-154 routeFor; js/modules/achievements.js:110-115 (reads arg as "tab/id"); js/core/files.js:146; js/core/search.js:115; js/modules/due.js:103-173
rootCause: Route codecs live in a central table in router.js that new views/args were not added to; routeFor silently drops unknown args.
fix: Add codecs for achievements (tab, set/<id>), assignments (id), reminders (id/section), review (tab, run) and cardstats; better, make each view declare its own route codec next to its KOS.views registration and have a smoke test round-trip every KOS.show call site through routeFor/parse.
detail: router.js only has ENCODE/DECODE entries for ref, subject, governor, code, japanese, creatives, mind, sims, money, routines, exams, goals, assistant, help, reports and pacing. Views that take an argument without a codec get a URL without it: KOS.show("achievements","titles") writes #/achievements, and the documented deep links #/achievements/sets|recent|showcase|titles|set/<id> (CLAUDE.md ownership map) all open on Sets (cold load of #/achievements/sets even rewrites the hash to #/achievements). KOS.show("assignments",{id}) (from Files' Where it's linked), KOS.show("reminders",{id,section}) (from search), KOS.show("review",{tab,run}) (Cram from the Exams Companion, Due today's queue buttons) and cardstats likewise. In-session Back works (argMemo keeps the arg per entry) but a reload, an iPad Home Screen app that iOS relaunched, or a copied link loses the place. This is also why a push notification opened from a cold start drops its object argument (see the earlier notification finding).

title: Nothing redraws the open page when the day changes: header clock says Mon 2 Nov, Home still says Sunday 1 November / Good evening
devices: all; most visible on the installed iPad app
evidence: shots/shell/bell-mac.png (clock 00:00 Mon 2 Nov vs hero Sunday 1 November); js/main.js:86-97 (only the clock ticks every 20 s); js/main.js:199-204 (30-min interval refreshes HUD and rail counters but never the view); hub.js:623 reads new Date() only when drawn
rootCause: Day-dependent views read new Date() only at draw time and the shell has no day-rollover redraw.
fix: In tickClock, remember the date string; when it changes (and on visibilitychange after a day boundary) call KOS.rerender() if no dialog/ink/Focus is busy (the rerender already waits on KOS.inkUI.busy).
detail: Left open across midnight (the user's installed iPad app is), the header clock ticks to the new date but the current view is never redrawn, so Home keeps yesterday's date line, greeting, Today list and daily goal until something else triggers a redraw. Observed at 00:00: header 'Mon 2 Nov', hero 'SUNDAY 1 NOVEMBER · Good evening', while the Week's plan card in the same page (drawn later) already read 'w/c 2 Nov'. A manual KOS.rerender() then showed 'Monday 2 November · Working late'.

title: Help on iPhone: section chips wrap into a ragged left-aligned cloud

rootCause: help.css nav reflows as flex-wrap at phone width.
fix: Use the shared scroller (one line, horizontally scrollable, declared overflow) or the phone title bar's section switch for the eight sections.

title: document.title never changes: every page, history entry and app-switcher card reads "Kurenai OS — Study Atelier"

Navigating to Money, Goals, a topic, Help etc. leaves the same title, so the browser history menu, Back long-press list, Safari tabs, the Mac window title and screen-reader page announcements cannot tell pages apart (WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled). Header controls are 40px (review chip), 38px (bell, Assistant), 32px (sync dot) and 34px brand at 1470px, so their centres and outlines don't line up; on iPhone the review chip is 44x40 beside 44x44 buttons (below the 44px coarse target).

title: ui.js still keeps a second, dead navigation stack (navHist/navFwd, KOS.back/forward/canBack) that the router overwrites
evidence: js/core/ui.js:325-336, :409-420, :1556-1562; js/core/router.js:248-251; document.getElementById('nav-back') === null
rootCause: The router was layered over ui.js's original stack without removing it.

title: iPad-portrait overlay rail: Escape does not close it, a tap on the page both closes it and activates what was under the finger, and its open state is persisted
evidence: eval at 820x1180: {s1:'full', focusIn:false, afterEsc:'full'}; js/main.js:71-81 (no Escape handler; stage pointerdown closes without preventing the click); :63-69 (setRail persists railOpenNarrow)

detail: At 701-1080px the opened rail floats over the page. Escape leaves it open (s1 'full' -> after Escape 'full'); focus stays on the toggle rather than entering the rail. The only dismissals are a destination or a pointerdown on #stage, and that pointerdown does not cancel the tap, so tapping the page to dismiss also presses whatever control was under the finger (tap-through). ui.railOpenNarrow is saved, so an overlay left open comes back open over the page on the next launch of the installed app.

title: iPad touch targets in the shell: the rail toggle is 24x24 and the collapsed rail buttons are 30px wide (narrower than their own 32px tile)
devices: iPad portrait (and iPad landscape for the toggle)
evidence: eval --size ipad: rail-toggle rect {x:59,y:76,w:24,h:24}; rail items [BUTTON,x21,w30,h44,padding 4px 0]; review chip 203x40; shots/shell/rail-tiles-ipad-crop.png; css/layout.css:213-235 (.k-rail-toggle 24px, coarse override to --hit-dense), :297-309 and :375 (tile 32px, item padding 4px 0)
rootCause: The dense-size exception was applied to the rail toggle to avoid an oval; the compact rail item has no minimum width.
fix: On coarse pointers give the rail toggle a 44px invisible hit area (a ::after inset that does not overlap the spine) or make it a 44px circle; give collapsed .k-rail-item min-inline-size: 44px (the rail is 71px wide); raise the header chip to the 44px touch height used by the other header controls.

The seven rail destinations measure 30x44: the button is narrower than the 32px kanji tile it contains (button min-inline-size:0 with padding 4px 0), so the hit area is smaller than what is drawn. The review chip in the header is 40px tall (under the 44px touch minimum).

title: A hidden live region announces a bare number ("545") at boot: #node-count is aria-live but only holds the total leaf count
evidence: eval mac: live regions [search-count:"", node-count:"545", kos-live-polite:"Routines", kos-live-assertive:""]; index.html:119; js/modules/hub.js:319-321
rootCause: Leftover live region from the pre-Graphite rail that showed a node count; violates invariant 66 (announce is the sole live-region route).
fix: Drop aria-live from #node-count (or delete the element: no reader uses it); invariant 66 already makes KOS.a11y.announce the sole live-region route.

A screen reader therefore says "545" (no words) shortly after the app loads, and again whenever the total changes (a curriculum release). Nothing else reads the element.

title: Hold-⌘ shortcut sheet is a fixed list: it shows Ink/PDF/Flashcard keys on every page and omits the shortcuts that exist (Backspace back, Esc, Money row keys, the Daily Review and routine player arrows and S, the story keys, the quiz arrow)

rootCause: SHORTCUTS is a hard-coded array in desk.js written for the iPad ink release; later features added keys without a place to declare them.
fix: Build the sheet from a registry: global keys plus a group contributed by the current view (KOS.desk.register(viewId, rows)); show only groups relevant to the page; align keys in a fixed-width column (grid) and use the 12-13px kbd token.
detail: Holding ⌘ on Home (no ink, no PDF, no cards on screen) shows the same four groups: Anywhere (/ and ⌥← ⌥→), Ink, A PDF, Flashcards. The app has more shortcuts than these and none is listed: Backspace = Back (main.js), Esc closes dialogs/menus/drawer, Money rows (Space ticks, E edits; money.js:607-609) and the month strip arrows (money.js:361), the Daily Review steps ← → (dayreview.js:181-182), the routine player ← → and S to skip (routineplayer.js:57-59), the report story ← → Space (reportstory.js:627-629), the quiz → for next (quiz.js:144). The key column is not aligned ("Page Up / Down" pushes its label to x=409 while the others start at x=404) and the kbd glyphs render at ~10px mono, smaller than the label text.

title: KOS.show with an unknown view id draws a blank page and pushes it into history (#/archive, #/nonsense) instead of falling back like a typed URL does

title: A ping shows on top of the unlock overlay (and above any dialog) when a tier and a ping arrive in the same sweep

title: Every Wall tab (and the Seat's showcase arc) waits 1.6-6 s on 'Reading your records…' because list() re-walks the whole vault each time
evidence: shots/achievements-governor/seed_showcase.png (blank 'Reading your records…' after 1.5 s); eval list() 4744 ms then 1623 ms; per-set timings above; js/core/achcatalogue.js:70-110 (openCursor over entries), js/core/achievements.js:329-341 (fresh makeCtx per list)
rootCause: Achievements are measured on read with no memo across calls; the Collection reader is a full-table cursor
fix: Cache the last evaluation's views (evaluate() already measures everything at boot and every 30 min and on owner touches) and draw the Wall from that cache immediately, refreshing in the background; for the vault, keep running tallies keyed on the vault's change notes or read counts through indexes (status/module) instead of a full cursor.
detail: Each Wall draw (Sets, Recent, Showcase, Titles, every tab switch since each is a KOS.show) calls KOS.achievements.list(), which makes a fresh context and re-measures all 254 badges; the Collection badges open an unbounded IndexedDB cursor over every vault entry (1,880 rows on the seeded account) and tally them. Timed on the seeded account: list() 1.6-4.7 s; per set sequentially: collection 6.5 s, exams 1.8 s, study 1.4 s, mind 1.3 s. Showcase still read 'Reading your records…' after 1.5 s. It also conflicts with invariant 8 (never read an unbounded collection).

title: Gold Shop: one tap on Buy spends the gold (up to 10,000) with no confirm and no undo, and equips the item at once
evidence: eval on #/governor/shop (mac, seeded): clicking [aria-label^="Buy Gilt ring"] → gold 12476 → 12386, no .k-dialog opened, toast "Bought Gilt ring. ◈ 12,386 left." with no action button; KOS.governor.refund/sell undefined. rootCause: buyWare treats purchase as instantly final and couples it with equip.
fix: Either confirm purchases above a threshold (e.g. ≥ 500 gold) through KOS.ui.confirm with the price and balance after, or keep one-tap but give the toast an Undo that refunds and restores the previously-used item within a few seconds. Consider not auto-equipping (or say "Bought and put on" so the swap is not a surprise).
detail: Every shop card has a Buy button that calls KOS.governor.buy directly: the gold is deducted, the item is owned and (for anything but a lab) immediately put in use by wareUse(it, true) — a new avatar, frame, seal, theme or outfit replaces what you had. title: Session Log shows a reward only for Focus (and re-prices it), never what quizzes, exams, cards, Code, Japanese, Mind or Creatives were paid; those four study spaces read as "Activity · Code · Code"
evidence: Fixture via eval: KOS.sessions.log focus (25 min pomodoro, 2 pauses) → award {xp:30,gold:4}; code → {0,0}; quiz (pct 80) → {xp:18,gold:10}. KOS.show(governor,history) rows: "18:52 | Quiz | Quiz completed | … · 80%" (no reward), "18:52 | Activity | Code | Code", "18:52 | Focus | Focus session completed | … · 25 min | +30 XP · +4 ◆". Code: js/modules/governor-ui.js:123-171 (activityInfo switch lacks code/ja/mind/creatives), 177-186 (rewardOf recomputes focus, null for everything else).
rootCause: The log predates the recorded award field and the newer study spaces; it was never extended.
fix: rewardOf: read s.award when present (any type; +0 shows nothing or No reward), fall back to focusAward only for pre-award entries. Add activityInfo cases for code (task/retrieval/capstone/project from metrics), ja (review session/lesson/checkpoint), mind and creatives with their own labels and details.
detail: Every session entry records what the Governor paid it (award {xp, gold}, invariant 100), but the Session Log's rewardOf() ignores it: Focus rows recompute the award through focusAward() from metrics (history is never to be re-priced, invariant 4a), Collection rows say "rest", and every other type shows no reward at all. A quiz logged in the fixture paid +18 XP +10 gold and its row shows only "Quiz completed · 80%". activityInfo() also has no case for the study spaces' own types (code, ja, mind, creatives), so their rows fall to the default: label "Activity", title = the capitalised type ("Code"), detail = the subject name ("Code") — a meaningless row. They also have category "study" by default so the Study filter works, but Japanese/Mind/Creatives get no distinguishing label. The header copy ("Open an entry for its recorded detail") promises the recorded record.

title: Recovery dispatch promises that ticking 2 plan items restores HP, but plan ticks move no HP at all
evidence: js/core/governor.js:946-973 (recoveryTasks: planTicks from state.pacing.entries, go → pacing / assignments), js/core/governor.js:278 (only todo pays hp 2), js/core/pacing.js:17 ("here calls KOS.sessions.log" — never; Pacing is logistics), js/modules/governor-ui.js:540-571 (copy "these three restore HP today").

Ticking plan items is Pacing's own bookkeeping with zero Governor traffic and zero sessions (invariant 82; pacing.js logs nothing), so doing that task changes HP by 0 while the checklist marks it done and advances the segments. Only Focus (+6 HP) and a reminder/assignment completion (todo, +2 HP) pay HP. Also: "Clear an overdue task" counts overdue reminders too, but its Start → only opens Assignments; and the copy says "these three" whatever HP will actually do.

title: Edit seat: choosing a title or a seal rebuilds the editor and drops keyboard focus to <body>; the radio groups have no arrow keys

fix: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. title: A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")
evidence: js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/core/edits.js:199-207 set() stores only the kind and updatedAt — no shipped hash or version; fixture: KOS.edits.set('maths','M7.3','notes', first 3 blocks) then reopen: no notice on the Notes tab or inspector (eval, then reset); shots/content-maths/top-m73-forked-mac.png taken after the reset shows the shipped 8 pages.
rootCause: The fork model has no notion of the base version it was taken from.
fix: Record a hash of the shipped kind on each fork (fork.base). When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". Check the user's real state for state.edits.topics['maths:M7.3'] (or 'maths:S7.3').
detail: KOS.content.get and srs read state.edits first (invariant 86). A fork copies the shipped material at the moment of the first edit and is never compared with the curriculum again. M7.3 was an outline entry until commit 4d791ca ("load M6–M7 at depth, drop their outline entries"), and a9f64b5 rewrote M7.2 and M7.3. A Notes fork made before then (or one carried over from S7.3 by the ref rename, router.js:117 renamedRef) keeps showing the old, thin outline notes. Nothing tells the user that a newer, much deeper version exists. The only sign is the Edit button's data-state forked (hub.js:2828). The shipped M7.3 renders in full (8 pages), so a bare M7.3 on the user's device most likely comes from such a fork.

title: Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5
evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 unchanged: answer says '$x_1 = 2.5$'; x1 = 0 − f(0)/f'(0) = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5.
rootCause: An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.
fix: Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).
detail: 9.3 FC5 (bank) asks "Why does $x_0 = 0$ fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" and answers "it does not fail here; $x_1 = 2.5$". In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.

title: Newton–Raphson generator prints a 'Root estimate' that is not a root in about a third of its random examples
evidence: eval on slot 7: 400 runs of KOS.worked.byIds(['newraph'])[0] → bad 138; examples quoted above; js/labs/worked.js:704 (Root estimate step printed unconditionally after three iterations)
fix: Iterate until |x_{n+1} − x_n| < 1e-6 (cap about 20) and show the first three steps plus 'converges to …'. Or pick x0 near a root (from a sign change). If it does not converge, say so ('not converged yet: f(x3) = …').
detail: The worked-example generator 'newraph', wired to 9.3, always does exactly three iterations from a random x0 and then prints 'Root estimate: x ≈ …', whatever f is at that point. In 138 of 400 random examples, |f(x3)| > 0.01. Two cases: x^3 − 2x − 5 from x0 = 1 gives 'x ≈ 3.34870 (f ≈ 25.85)' (the true root is 2.0946), and x^3 + x − 1 from x0 = 3 gives 'x ≈ 0.88069 (f ≈ 0.564)' (the true root is 0.6823). A learner using the generator to check their own working is taught that a non-converged value is the answer.

title: 'Retry the N missed' overwrites the topic's quiz score with the retry's: 9/13 then 4/4 records lastPct 100 and the head reads 'best 9/4'
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/qz-retry.js (eval on slot 7, output quoted); shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png ('best 9/13', inspector 'Quiz attempts 2', 'Data says Green'); js/engines/quiz.js:156-165, :178-181; js/modules/rag.js:63-71
rootCause: The missed-retry reuses mountMCQ's normal finish path, which assumes items is the topic's whole quiz.
fix: Pass a 'practice' flag for the missed retry: do not touch st.lastPct/best (or record it under a separate missedRetry field), log it as a practice session (or not at all), and print the head as 'retrying 4 missed' instead of best/total.
detail: After a quiz, 'Retry the N missed' (js/engines/quiz.js:178-181) mounts the SAME engine on the missed subset with the topic's own stats record. finish() (quiz.js:156-160) then sets lastPct = correct / subset size, logs a second 'quiz' session with total = the subset, and the head line compares the stored best (a count out of the full quiz) with the subset length. Repro on #/ref/maths/M7.3 (empty account): answer every question with A → 9/13, record {attempts 1, best 9, lastPct 69}; press 'Retry the 4 missed', answer them right → record {attempts 2, best 9, lastPct 100}, sessions [{9/13 69%}, {4/4 100%}], head 'score 4 · best 9/4'. RAG reads lastPct (js/modules/rag.js:63-71), so a learner who got 69% now shows no quiz weakness at all, and the ledger/Reports count a 100% quiz that never happened.

title: One mediocre quiz makes a Maths topic 'Data says Green': the RAG starts at 100 and a 69% quiz only takes 8 points off
evidence: shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png; js/modules/rag.js:17 (band), :63-71 (quiz penalty capped at 25), :103 (no minimum evidence); eval qz-retry.js before the retry: lastPct 69 → band g
rootCause: Subtractive scoring from 100 with capped penalties and no evidence threshold.
fix: Make the auto band evidence-weighted: start from 'no claim' and require a minimum amount of evidence (e.g. ≥ N cards rated or a quiz ≥ 80 % plus another signal) before Green; map a lone quiz to a score proportional to its percentage rather than a capped deduction.
detail: rag.auto (js/modules/rag.js:30-110) starts every topic at score 100 and SUBTRACTS for weak signals; band() (rag.js:17) is Green from 70. With only a quiz as evidence, the most a quiz can remove is 25 (lastPct 0 %), so ANY single quiz attempt — even 0 % — leaves the topic Amber or Green, and a 69 % quiz removes 8 → Green. Thin evidence (one quiz, no cards rated, no exam questions, 0/4 checks, status Not started) is judged as mastery. Repro: empty account, M7.3, quiz answered all-A (9/13 = 69 %): inspector shows 'Data says Green' beside 'Not started' and '0/4 checks'. The answer-position bias (all-A scores 69 %) makes this reachable without reading a single question.

title: Normal-distribution generator writes the symmetric interval backwards, e.g. P(61 < X < 51)
evidence: eval on slot 7: normal solve with {mu:56,sg:2,x:51} → 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876 (symmetric interval about μ)'; js/labs/worked.js:549
fix: Print P(min(x, 2μ−x) < X < max(x, 2μ−x)).
detail: When the random x is below μ (89 of 200 runs), the 'Complements you might need' step prints P(2μ − x < X < x). Example: X ~ N(56, 2²), x = 51 gives 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876'. That is an empty interval written as if it were the answer.

title: Hypothesis-test generators draw contradictory set-ups (testing p < p0 with x far above the mean)
evidence: eval on slot 7 (400-run sweeps of every one of the 36 Maths generators: no exceptions or NaN; hyptestSilly 187/400; projectile '−0' 174/400); js/labs/worked.js:752 (hyptest random); js/labs/worked-extra.js:356-373 (projectile)
fix: hyptest: draw x from the alternative's side (below n·p0 for 'lower'), and draw h in the projectile generator only when h > 0 or drop the term. Use a shared signed formatter that brackets negatives inside a product or after a minus sign.
detail: The 'hyptest' generator (S5.2) draws the tail and x independently. In 187 of 400 random examples, x lies on the wrong side of the mean for the alternative being tested. Example: H1: p < 0.4 with n = 17 and x = 15 gives P(X ≤ 15) = 1.00000. The example is formally right but teaches nothing, and no exam question is set up that way. The projectile generator also prints '−0 = 20T − 4.9T²' and '4.9T² − 20T − 0 = 0' whenever h = 0 (174 of 400 runs). The partial-fractions and normal-parameters generators print unbracketed double signs: '(5·-1 + -1) / (-1 − 1)' and 'μ = 25 − -0.9945 × 8.0963'.

title: SQL tasks: a slow first SQLite load fails a correct answer as an infinite loop, and the kill makes every retry cold again
evidence: eval: Check on #/code/task/T1.2-recent after reload → tests pane text quoted above (12339 ms); eval: two consecutive KOS.codeRun.run SQL calls → both {code:'TIMEOUT', msg:'Stopped after 4 seconds.'}; raw new Worker('js/labs/sql-worker.js') → 16295 ms, res.ms 4080. Code: js/core/coderun.js:199-203 (timeout → sqlKill → next run fresh), :174-177; js/core/codeui.js:256-257 (hard-coded '2 seconds' and loop advice for every timeout); js/data/code.js:424
rootCause: Watchdog covers worker boot + run together and kills the booted worker; error copy assumes C#
fix: Separate loading from running: post a warm-up message and wait for a 'ready' reply before starting the per-run watchdog (or show 'Loading SQLite…' while it loads); on a timeout keep the loaded worker when the run never started; make the timeout card language-aware (no loop advice for SQL) and print the real limit.
detail: On a fresh page, pressing Check on T1.2-recent with the task's own answer took 12 s and reported 'Case 1 · 4000 ms · ✗ Did not finish · Stopped after 2 seconds in case 1 · Did not finish — is there a loop whose condition never becomes false? · Usually because: a loop whose condition never becomes false' — C# loop advice for a one-line SELECT. KOS.codeRun.run({lang:'sql', src:'SELECT 1;'}) right after a reload timed out (13.9 s) and so did the next call (10.4 s): sqlRun's watchdog calls sqlKill(), which sets sqlw = null, so the following run is 'fresh' again and pays the whole SQLite load once more. Only when a load happens to finish inside the 8 s window does SQL work (a later Check passed and paid). In this audit harness the raw sql-worker took 16 s to answer its first query (query itself 4.08 s), so the harness CPU was slow — but the logic means a slow device (an iPad on battery, a phone) can stay stuck failing every SQL task, and the message blames the learner's code. The timeout figures are also wrong: the card hard-codes '2 seconds' while the wait was 4 s (warm) or 8 s (cold).

title: 'Held in reviews' (4th lesson check) is never written to the progress record by reviews, so the inspector shows 3/4 · 75% while the stored status, spine and unit counts stay behind
evidence: eval: after reading all 8 pages of 1.1, finishLesson, and holding every item's R facet (reps 3, s 30): KOS.ja.evidence('1.1').checks = [true,false,true,true] but KOS.store.peekProgress('ja','1.1').check = [true,false,true,false] (also after rendering the topic page). rootCause: Evidence that changes through the scheduler has no write path into the progress record
fix: After KOS.ja.record()/finishSession(), call syncChecks for every lesson whose items were reviewed (map item → lesson), and run a one-pass syncChecks over all started lessons at boot (as Code's syncChecks is run), so the stored checks always equal evidence().
detail: KOS.ja.syncChecks is called only from markPage, markHeard and finishLesson (js/core/ja.js:106,112,241) — never from record()/finishSession() or at boot. The 4th check (every item's R/L facet reps ≥ 2 and s ≥ 7) can only become true later, through review sessions, so it is never synced unless the learner happens to open an unread page or play an unheard line of that lesson afterwards. The inspector computes evidence live and shows the check ticked and '3 of 4 checks 75%', while the shared progress record (which drives the status select 'Started', the spine's 'F1 0 / 6', 'Kana to native media 0 / 28 completed', the subject's mastery in Home/Reports/Goals and the auto Completed status) keeps check[3] = false. A lesson can therefore never reach Completed through reviews.

title: Japanese learn session asks Listening first and buries every Reading facet (sibling tie-break sorts 'L' before 'R')

Root: js/core/jasrs.js:105-107 sort tie-break (a.k < b.k) puts '|L' before '|R' when over and recall are equal (new facets: 0, 0), then :110-111 keeps only the first facet of each item.
rootCause: Alphabetical key tie-break in the sibling-burying queue
fix: In queue(), break ties by skill order (R, L, W, S, H) before the key string, or in jarun.run for a learn session take the lesson's facets from KOS.ja.peek().facets directly rather than the sibling-buried due() list.
detail: Start lesson 1.1 on an empty account: KOS.ja.due() returns j:本|R and then only the |L facet of every word and pattern (w:これ|L, g:ka|L, …); every |R facet is buried as a sibling. jarun.run then sorts 'Reading before Listening', but the R facets were already removed, so a brand-new word is met and immediately asked by ear (listen-pick: hear it, pick the meaning) with no reading check at all on day one. The code's stated intent (jarun.js:369 'the lesson's own facets, Reading first') is not what happens.

title: Sibling rule broken within a day: once one facet of an item is answered, its buried sibling becomes due the same day
evidence: eval: KOS.ja.record('w:これ|L', {verdict:'correct',ms:2000}) then KOS.ja.due().indexOf('w:これ|R') >= 0 → true (same day 2026-11-05). js/core/jasrs.js:101-114 filters only by f.due <= today; no check of a sibling's f.last === today.
rootCause: Burying is computed over the current due set only, with no 'reviewed today' memory
fix: In queue(), skip a facet whose sibling has last === today (unless both are >2 days overdue), or push the buried sibling's due to tomorrow when its sibling is reviewed in record().
detail: Invariant 113: 'Two facets of one item never share a day unless both are over two days overdue.' queue() only buries a sibling among facets that are due at the same moment; it keeps no memory of what was reviewed today. After answering w:これ|L (due moves to +10 days), w:これ|R is the item's only due facet, so the next session the same day (or 'Reviews' from the desk straight after the lesson) asks it.

title: One fast correct answer unlocks the Writing facet at once: 'R holds a week' is read as first-review stability ≥ 7 days, which a single Easy gives (s 8.3)
evidence: eval after startLesson('1.1'): KOS.ja.record('w:これ|R',{verdict:'correct',hints:0,ms:2000}).unlocked = ['w:これ|W']; KOS.ja.record('g:ka|R',{…ms:3000}).unlocked = ['g:ka|W']; facet after one answer {s: 8.2956, ivl: 10}. js/core/jasrs.js:62 held = r.reps && r.s >= HOLD; js/core/jasrs.js:45 a correct answer within target → 4 (Easy) regardless of tries; js/core/ja.js:35 TARGET R 4000 ms.
rootCause: Stability used as a proxy for elapsed holding time

title: Mind ladder: most F1 concepts can never climb past Recall/Apply — 5 of 16 concepts have no route to any rung above Recall, only 3 can reach Evaluate
evidence: eval over KOS_MIND (slot 11): 'premise E[] A[] V[]', 'deduction E[] A[] V[]', 'straw-man E[] A[] V[]', 'false-dilemma E[] A[] V[]', 'bandwagon E[] A[] V[]', 'soundness E[] A[F1.3#2] V[]', 'standard-form E[F1.2] A[] V[]', 'steelman E[] A[F1.7#1] V[F1.7,cp]'; rules in js/core/mind.js:278-318 (ladder); hero bars js/modules/mind.js:66-72; furthest js/core/mind.js:497-503
rootCause: Ladder rules require per-concept evidence sources that the F1 content file only provides for the lesson 'main' concepts; nothing checks reachability.
fix: Either author a route for every rung of every concept (apply items for each fallacy/premise/deduction; explain-back key points or checkpoint rubric rows for the rest), or let a concept declare which rungs it has (`rungs: ['Recall','Apply']`) and draw/count only those, computing the hero bars and 'furthest' over reachable rungs. smoke110 should assert every concept has a source for every rung it shows.
detail: The ladder (invariant 137) is derived from four evidence sources: Explain = an explain-back on a lesson whose `main` is the concept, or a checkpoint rubric row; Apply = a check/checkpoint item marked `apply` for the concept; Evaluate = a position on a contested lesson teaching the concept, or an Evaluate rubric row. Enumerating F1's authored content against those rules: premise, deduction, straw-man, false-dilemma and bandwagon have NO Explain, Apply or Evaluate source (they can only ever reach Recall); conclusion, soundness, ad-hominem, slippery-slope reach Recall+Apply only; standard-form has Explain but no Apply; steelman has no Explain (F1.7 is contested, so its prompt is a position). Only induction, charity and steelman can reach Evaluate. Yet every met concept is drawn with four rungs, the desk hero shows 'Evaluate 0%' bars computed over all met concepts and 'furthest' needs half the met concepts on a rung — so a learner who does every piece of F1 perfectly still sees Explain ≈ 38%, Evaluate ≈ 19% and four-rung ladders that cannot be completed, with no hint why.

title: Evaluate is lost whenever a position is revised: the revise sheet starts with an empty objection/reply and the ladder reads only the latest version
evidence: eval (slot 11): takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,objection:'o',reply:'y'}) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] true, ladder('charity').rungs[3] true; then takePosition('F1.7',{answer:1,conf:60,reason:'r2'}) (what the revise sheet sends when the objection is not retyped) → ladder('steelman').rungs[3] false
rootCause: ladder uses only the latest version; position() sheet does not carry the objection forward
fix: Evaluate should hold if ANY version (or any non-retired position) has an objection answered; and pre-fill the revise sheet's objection/reply from the previous version (open the details when present).
detail: ladder() grants Evaluate from `latest(lid)` having both objection and reply (js/core/mind.js:308-312). The position sheet pre-fills answer, confidence and reason from the previous version but always starts objection and reply as '' (js/modules/mindrun.js:96 `objection: "", reply: ""`), and the objection <details> is closed. So a learner who answered an objection in v1 and later revises (e.g. a revisit's 'Revise', or nudging confidence) without retyping it drops the concept back below Evaluate — for every concept the contested lesson teaches (F1.7: steelman AND charity). The saved card then shows the ladder without Evaluate and no message says it was lost. An 'earned' rung going away on an unrelated edit contradicts 'every rung comes from evidence' (the earlier evidence still exists in version history).

title: Checkpoint pays 50 XP / 12 gold / +4 HP and marks itself passed with nothing right; a retake then erases the Explain/Evaluate rungs it gave
evidence: eval (slot 11): recordCheckpoint('F1',{cards:0,apply:{},synth:{bullets:['x'],ticks:{0:true,2:true}}}) → {paid:true}, governor 0/0 → 50/12; ledger [F1.8,{kind:'checkpoint',first:true},{xp:50,gold:12}]; ladder('argument').rungs[1] true, ladder('induction').rungs[3] true; retake recordCheckpoint('F1',{synth:{bullets:['y'],ticks:{}}}) → both false
rootCause: recordCheckpoint has no pass condition and replaces the record on every attempt
fix: Define a pass rule (e.g. ≥ 2 of 3 scenarios right and ≥ half the rubric) and pay only on the first PASS, saying what is missing otherwise; keep the best attempt (merge apply/ticks by OR, or store attempts and read the best) so a retake never lowers a rung.
detail: recordCheckpoint() always sets doneAt and pays the first time (js/core/mind.js:382-405); the UI's only gate is one non-empty synthesis bullet (js/modules/mind.js:562). Cards are self-marked 'Had it/Not quite' and apply scenarios can all be wrong — 0 of 8 cards, 0 of 3 scenarios, 0 rubric points and a one-character bullet still pay the full checkpoint reward and tick F1.8's 'Check passed'. (Japanese's checkpoint requires 80% in every skill; the Mind plan's 'unit checkpoint 50/12/+4' reads as a passed checkpoint.) Separately, Retake overwrites `apply` and `synth.ticks` wholesale, so a retake with fewer rubric ticks removes Explain (argument, hidden-premise) and Evaluate (induction, steelman) that the first attempt earned.

title: Apply and Explain rungs are earned without showing understanding: Apply after the check has revealed the answer, Explain from one one-character bullet
evidence: eval (slot 11): answerCheck('F1.3',3,0) → ok:false, ladder('validity').apply 0; answerCheck('F1.3',3,1) → ok:true, apply 1, rungs [F,F,T,F]; saveExplain('F1.3',['x'],{0:1,1:1,2:1}) → {reached:true,ticked:3,of:4} with evidence('F1.3').read 0 of 6
rootCause: answerCheck records ok on any later right answer; saveExplain trusts ticks with no text threshold
fix: Count Apply only when the scenario is right at the FIRST attempt of a visit (or on a later day, with the answer not revealed in the same session); for a retried item show 'Right, but it counts next time'. For Explain require a minimum (e.g. ≥ 3 bullets or ~20 words) before ticks count, and order the prompt after the pages.
detail: Leniency of the derived ladder with thin evidence: (1) Apply = 'a scenario answered right'. A wrong answer immediately marks the right option '✓ Right' (js/modules/mindtopic.js:103-106) and offers 'Next, and come back to this'; coming back, clicking the option that was just revealed records ok:true (answerCheck keeps the first ok) and the concept reaches Apply — so every Apply rung (and the check pass that pays 12 XP) can be had by guessing once. (2) Explain = ≥60% of key points self-ticked; the text itself is not checked at all, so a single bullet 'x' with 3 of 4 ticks reaches Explain, and the explain-back can be written before a single page is read.

rootCause: Batch metadata is not stored anywhere but on rows; UI only exposes it in a transient dialog.
fix: An 'Imports' list (Transactions › Imports or Settings): file name, date range, rows, when imported, with Undo/Delete and 'Replace with a new file'. Store {batch, fileName, from, to, n, at} in state.money.imports. Add a Source filter and Select all in view.
detail: Undo works only on the Done step (verified: 3 imported → Undo → 0). No other caller of undoBatch, no batch/source filter in list(), no select-all in the bulk bar. — Each import has a batch id, but 'Undo this import' exists only on the Done step of the dialog (money.js:915). Once closed there is no import history, no filter by source/batch in Transactions (list() filters kind/cat/tag/search only), and bulk select has no 'select all' over a range, so removing a bad 200-row import means ticking rows one by one.

gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
title: Unquoted thousands separators shift columns: '£1,234.56' imports silently as £1.00
rootCause: Parser trusts column positions without validating row width.
fix: Flag rows whose cell count differs from the header ('Row 3 has 6 cells, the header has 5'), and for the known Santander layout re-join a split £n,nnn.nn amount; show the running Balance column so a mismatch is visible.
detail: parse of 'Date,Description,Amount,Balance' + '27/10/2026,STUDENT FINANCE,£1,234.56,£1,500.00' gives 6 cells for a 4-column header and previews as ['in', 100] (£1.00). — A comma-delimited bank file that writes amounts like £1,234.56 without quotes (common in hand-rolled UK exports, and what users get after re-saving midata in a text editor) splits the amount into two cells. The parser never checks a row's cell count against the header, so the Student Finance row imported as +£1.00 and the balance column swallowed '234.56'. No warning in the preview.

gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
title: A recurring rule's 'Confirm' and an imported bank row for the same payment double-count
evidence: js/core/money.js:414-433, 1025-1031; eval t3.js confirmVsImport {dup:false}; #/money/recurring due card 'Student Finance · £450.00 | Due · 12 days ago'
rootCause: Rules and imports are two independent writers of the same real-world payment.
fix: On import, match rows to due occurrences (same amount ±0, date within ±3 days, payee alias set on the rule) and MARK the occurrence done pointing at the imported tx instead of creating a new one; on Confirm, offer 'Use the bank entry from 27 Oct' when one matches.
detail: Fixture: rule 'Google One' £1.59 confirmed for 20 Jan, then a bank row '20/01/2027, GOOGLE *Google One, ON 19-01-2027, -1.59' previews duplicate:false and would import as a second £1.59. Seeded data shows the same for Student Finance (typed £450 on 27 Oct and the rule's 27 Oct occurrence still 'Due · 12 days ago' with a 'Received £450.00' button). — Confirming an occurrence (Google One £1.59, Phone £10) writes its own transaction r:<rule>:<date> with payee = rule name; importing the bank statement then adds 'GOOGLE *Google One, ON 27-10-2026' £1.59 as a separate row. Neither side looks at the other: preview's dedupe compares payee text ('google one' vs the bank string) and confirm() never searches existing transactions. Spend, budgets, Safe to spend and Reports count the payment twice. This is a second path to the duplicates the user saw.

gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
title: Imported rows are unusable as information: raw bank strings, everything in Other, Type and Balance columns discarded
evidence: js/core/money.js:1019-1021, 1041; js/modules/money.js:962 (map options: date/payee/amount/out/in/note only); dialog map ['Type=>','Balance=>']
rootCause: Import engine was built as a column copier ('the pages are phase 2' comment at money.js:946).
fix: Revamp (see summary): store raw text, derive a clean merchant (strip 'CARD PAYMENT TO', '(VIA APPLE PAY)', ', ON dd-mm-yyyy', ',n.nn GBP, RATE …', store numbers, title-case); payee rules {match -> merchant, category} learned when the user sets a category ('Always put Heron Foods in Food?'); a built-in UK merchant table (Tesco, Heron Foods, Greggs, Stagecoach, Google, Spotify, SLC…); Type DD/SO -> suggest a recurring rule; Balance -> reconcile and show 'Matches the bank: £120.10'.
detail: Workaround import (renamed headers) stores payee 'HERON FOODS HOYLAND (VIA APPLE PAY), ON 29-10-2026', cat 'other'; Type and Balance mapped to 'Leave out' with no option to use them. — Every imported row lands in Other/Other income (preview opts.outCat), payee is the raw bank text ('HERON FOODS HOYLAND (VIA APPLE PAY), ON 29-10-2026', 'CARD PAYMENT TO …,3.45 GBP, RATE 1.00/GBP ON …'), so Overview's 'This month by category' is one 'Other' bar, the Selected card shows a 4-line shouting title, spend-by-merchant is impossible and nothing learns from the user's re-categorising. The bank's Type (DEB/DD/FPI/FPO/SO) and Balance columns are dropped, so direct debits are not detected and the import cannot be reconciled. There is no merchant normalisation, no payee->category memory and no recurring detection anywhere in money.js.

gverdict: confirmed by Claude's independent re-check (B2, runtime + code)
reviewNote: Mitigation: each flagged row has an 'Import anyway' toggle, but Skip is pre-selected and the row claims to match an entry that is not in the store.
title: Two genuine identical payments on the same day in one statement: the second is marked 'Already have' and skipped by default
evidence: js/core/money.js:1027-1031 (keys[k] = true inside the file loop); eval of the import dialog with money-samples/midata-workaround.csv: pv row 2 '≈ Already have … matches an entry on 29 Oct Skip'
rootCause: Within-file repeats are deliberately folded into the duplicate set.

detail: previewCSV adds every row's key (date|amount|payee) to the seen set as it goes ('a repeat inside the same file is a duplicate too'), so two real card payments of the same amount at the same shop on the same day (two meal deals, two bus fares) are treated as one: the preview shows the second as '≈ Already have · matches an entry on 29 Oct' with Skip pre-selected, and Import imports one. title: Re-importing the app's own CSV export turns every outgoing into income and files the category as a note
evidence: js/core/money.js:973-977 (note: /category/), 1005-1013 (sign from the minus), 1058-1076 (export unsigned + Type); eval: roundtrip kinds {in: 40}, pv[0] ['2026-10-01','in',1438,'Steam','Other']

title: Painted page header shows the PREVIOUS page's picture (Goals shows Money's jar, Money shows Goals' mountain)
evidence: eval hdr.js imgs per route (mac and ipad); js/core/ui.js:589-592, 1540-1543; shots/money-goals/r2-goals-week-empty-mac.png (Money's jar on Goals)
rootCause: Ordering in KOS.show: state.ui.view assigned after render.

title: Amounts written as (3.45) or 3.45 DR import as money in
evidence: js/core/money.js:63-70; dialog preview of money-samples/odd-amounts.csv: 'PAREN NEG +£3.45', 'DR SUFFIX +£3.45', row 5 'no amount'

title: Editing a transfer into a move between two pots keeps the original and adds two new entries

title: Money goals are met with no evidence: 'No-spend days' counts days with no entries at all, and 'Spend under' is met by an empty month
evidence: js/core/goals.js:680-711; empty account (reset), goals added via KOS.goals.add: #/goals text '✓ Met | 5 no-spend days | 7 | of 5 days | Met. Nothing more to do here.' and 'Your run … 2 met this week'; shots/money-goals/r2-goals-thin-mac.png; shots/money-goals/r2-overview-dawn-mac.png (chip '7 no-spend days', '1 day so far')
rootCause: Absence of data is read as absence of spending.
fix: Require evidence that Money is in use for the period (entries on at least N days, or an import covering the range) before judging; otherwise read 'Not enough entries to judge'. Start counting from the goal's creation day.
detail: money-no-spend counts every day of the period up to today on which no 'out' entry exists, so on an account with zero Money entries a weekly '5 no-spend days' goal created today reads '✓ Met · 7 of 5 days · Met. Nothing more to do here.' (it also counts days before the goal existed). money-spend-under reads 0 spent for a month with no entries and will be judged met at the end of the period. A user who simply did not log spending is told they kept their goal, and the outcome is stored in the goal's history. The Overview makes the same claim: its chip read '7 no-spend days' on a month with entries on one day, while Safe to spend in the same hero says it needs 7 days WITH entries — the two disagree about what an empty day means.

title: Budgets: the Payday day picker does nothing while the month starts on the 1st, then Payday ignores the day you picked

Its change handler only saves when monthStart is already not 1, so a user on The 1st who picks 15th sees the select change but nothing is saved, and pressing Payday then sets the 28th. detail: The review notice is pushed with view 'routines' and arg {review: slot}. KOS.notify.open() calls KOS.show('routines', {review:'morning'}), but KOS.views.routines only reads arg.edit or a tab string, so the arg is dropped and the page shows Routines › Today. The review sheet does not open; the user has to find the header chip. The same item reaches the bell, the Notifications page and closed-app pushes (sw notificationclick → kos-open → KOS.show), so all three dead-end.

title: History's 'Open Account & Cloud Sync' button opens the Collection's Sync & Import page, which has no sign-in

detail: Assistant › History, signed out, shows 'History is kept after cloud sign-in' with a button 'Open Account & Cloud Sync'. It calls KOS.show('mediasync'), the Collection's Sync & Import page (AniList, VNDB, Games…), which has no email/password fields. The sign-in card lives on Archive › Backup & Restore (#/data). The user lands on the wrong page with no way forward.

title: Every 'sign in first' message points to 'Archive → Account & Cloud Sync', a page that does not exist, and offers no button
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/chat-send-signedout-mac.png; shots/assistant-archive/memory-mac.png; js/core/ai.js:152,154; js/modules/assistant.js:2299; js/core/cloud.js:142-143; js/core/gameapi.js:23,25; js/core/vndb.js:112,281; js/core/ui.js:430-438 (Archive strip names)
rootCause: Navigation text duplicated in many string literals instead of one link helper; page renamed in review A
fix: Name it as the UI does ('Archive › Backup & Restore › Account & Cloud Sync') and render an inline 'Sign in' action on the Assistant error card and the Memory/History empty states that opens #/data with the email field focused. Signed out with no Ollama model, show a one-line notice above the composer before the first send instead of failing after it.
detail: The Assistant's failure card (signed out, the default Gemini route), Memory's empty state, cloud.js, gameapi.js and vndb.js all say 'Archive → Account & Cloud Sync'. The Archive has no page of that name: the strip reads Backup & Restore, Help & Guide, Notifications, Files, Storage, Pen and ink, Connections; the card is a section inside Backup & Restore. Connections calls it 'Open Backup & cloud'. None of the Assistant's messages is a link. A first-time user who types a question gets 'Kurenai couldn't finish that' with directions to a page they cannot find, while the status pill still says 'Kurenai is with you' with a green dot.

title: Activity (signed out) shows every action as 'Proposed … Started' forever, with no time
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/activity-after-mac.png (after a todo_add_task that the chat reported complete). js/modules/assistant.js:2587-2590 (filter r.kind === 'insert'); js/core/aiorchestrator.js:232-250 (status changes are separate 'update' rows; the insert payload has no created_at)
rootCause: Queue reader ignores update rows; insert payload lacks a timestamp
fix: When reading the queue, fold each 'update' patch into its insert by id and use the queue entry's ts as created_at.
detail: Signed out, Activity reads the local audit queue but keeps only the 'insert' rows and drops every 'update' (executed/declined/failed), so an action that ran reads 'Proposed', 'todo_add_task · proposed' and '● Started' in one row. The queued rows have no created_at, so the 'when' column is an empty 100px gap at the row's left. The filters Ran / Declined / Failed never match anything signed out.

title: Restoring a backup MERGES handwriting instead of replacing it (every other store is cleared first)
evidence: rt18/ink2.js result inkDocs ['topic:cs:4.1.1','topic:cs:4.1.2'] vs money ['tA','tB']; js/core/ink.js:531-541 (no clear) vs js/core/money.js:1097, js/core/mediadb.js:1373-1374, js/core/reviewlog.js:108, js/core/mindjournal.js:167, js/core/creatives.js:467
rootCause: ink.importAll was written as an additive put, unlike the shared clear-then-put pattern of the other importAll functions.
fix: Clear docs, pages, base and dead (and reset the in-memory index) in ink.importAll before putting the backup's pages, like the other stores.
detail: A full restore is documented as a replace. Media, files, money, reviews, Mind and Creatives importAll all clear their stores first; KOS.ink.importAll only puts, so notebooks/pages that exist on the device but not in the backup survive, and the ink sync base/dead stores are left describing pages the restore may have changed. Reproduced: an extra ink doc topic:cs:4.1.2 added before import is still there afterwards while the extra money transaction was removed.

title: Full backup leaves out saved Reports (weeks, months, words) and Money pot pictures, so a restore loses them
evidence: Round trip: /tmp/kosqa18-before.json reports 11 -> after restore 5 (keys month:2026-09, month:2026-10, week:2026-10-12/19/26); backup keys = state, mediaEntries, mediaKV, attachments, creatives, ink, mind, money{tx,del}, reviews; js/core/store.js:513-585 (no reportStore / pics step); js/core/money.js:1079-1090 exports TX/DEL only
rootCause: Each new IndexedDB was added to the backup by hand; reports and pot pictures were missed and nothing checks the backup covers every kurenai-os-* database.
fix: Add KOS.reportStore.exportAll/importAll (reports + snapshots) and the money pics store to snapshotFull/importFull and the report list in the toast; update the Data page's 'What a backup covers'.
detail: snapshotFull serialises state, media, files, money tx, reviews, Mind, ink and creatives, but not kurenai-os-reports (saved reports and boundary snapshots, which invariant 101/102 say are saved once and never recomputed, including Kurenai-written words) nor kurenai-os-money's 'pics' store (a pot's own picture). Round trip on the seeded account: 11 saved reports before, 5 after restore into an empty slot (all September and early-October weeks gone; only those the app could re-backfill came back, now without their original snapshots/words); pics never appear in the file. Signed-out users (no kos_reports replication) lose them permanently.

title: Scheduled tab's day buttons are 32x44 ovals on iPad and iPhone
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/sched-ipad.png; DOM measure at ipad and iphone: every 'Monday'..'Sunday' button 32x44; css/views/assistant.css:464 (.k-asst-day inline-size: var(--hit) with border-radius 50%)

title: Toggling a notification filter (or any Notifications switch) redraws the page and drops keyboard focus to <body>
evidence: eval: after clicking the 'Calendar notifications' switch swStill:false, activeElement MAIN; after 'Daily Review' activeElement BODY; js/modules/notifications.js:320-321, js/core/notify.js:102-108 (emit), :115-119
rootCause: The notify change event triggers a full view rebuild instead of a targeted update, with no focus restoration.
fix: Update the switch and counts in place (or restore focus by data-ui/aria-label after the redraw, as KOS.rerender does for other views).
detail: Each switch on #/notifications (Notification filters, Device alerts, Quiet hours) calls KOS.notify.setMuted/setQuiet, which emits and the whole view is rebuilt; the switch the user just pressed is replaced, so focus falls to MAIN/BODY. A keyboard or switch-control user toggling 15 filters must tab back from the top after every one. Scroll position is kept.

title: Help & Guide is badly out of date: no entry for the Assistant, Money, Goals, Reports, Exams hub, Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives, Achievements or Connections, and several entries describe removed features
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/help-seed-mac.png, help-iphone.png; eval guide search: {japanese:'Nothing matches', assistant:'Nothing matches', money:['Kurenai\'s words'], goal:['Planner']}; js/modules/help.js:9-110 (SECTIONS), :11, :13, :57, :61, :79, :106
rootCause: Help is a hand-maintained array with no test tying it to the registered views, so each release added pages without guide entries.
fix: Add a section per study space and per Productivity/Archive page added since (Assistant, Money, Goals, Reports, Exams hub, Achievements, Connections, Wishlist), rewrite the stale entries, give every section a kanji, and add a smoke check that every rail view has a Help entry.
detail: The guide's eight sections stop at roughly the Collection/Pacing era. Searching 'japanese' or 'assistant' returns 'Nothing matches'; 'money' finds only 'Kurenai's words'; 'goal' finds only 'Planner', which still says 'The Planner workspace holds Budget Planner and Goals under one secondary tab bar' (gone: invariant 27). Other stale text: Overview describes 'overall completion ring, today's to-do... flagged topics' (Home is Up next / Today / Upcoming / Today's three now); search covers 'all three subjects' (there are seven study spaces); 'Today's directives... Ticks earn XP'; Cloud Sync lives at 'Archive → Account & Cloud Sync'; Gold omits the picture-upload unlocks (roadmap 5.14); section names 'The Behavioural Governor' and 'The Collection Matrix' no longer match the rail (Governor, Collection › Overview); 'Data & housekeeping' has a '·' instead of a kanji mark. Invariant 50a sends readers to Help for rules, so the gaps matter.

title: After a backup restore the rail's profile card and the file index stay stale (Level 1, 0 gold; 'No files on this device yet')
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/data-seed-mac.png (rail card Level 1 / 0 gold vs 'Level 53 · ◆12,476' in What a backup covers); shots/assistant-archive/storage-seed-mac.png; eval {g:{xp:71802,gold:12476}, lvl:53, card:'Your profile — Level 1, Healthy, 0 gold'}; eval KOS.files.all().length 0 before refresh, 1 after; js/modules/hub.js:3370-3372; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-731
rootCause: Each in-memory cache (HUD, files index) is refreshed only by its own events; replaceState has no broadcast that the caches subscribe to.
fix: Give restore and remote-apply one 'state replaced' hook that calls refreshHUD, KOS.files.refresh, the theme apply and the rail counters (or simply reload the page after a restore, as the safest complete answer).
detail: importFull replaces the state and the IndexedDBs in place and the Data page then calls only refreshRailCounters and KOS.show('home'). KOS.refreshHUD is never called, so the rail/phone profile card keeps the pre-restore Governor (here 'Level 1, Healthy, 0 gold' while the restored state is level 53 with 12,476 gold) until a session is logged or the app reloads; and KOS.files' in-memory index is not rebuilt, so Storage says 'No files on this device yet' / 'Every file is linked somewhere' and Files is empty although the restored notes.txt is in kurenai-os-files (KOS.files.all() = 0 until KOS.files.refresh()). Cloud pulls take the same path (cloudsync.js rerenderCurrent: refreshRailCounters + rerender, no refreshHUD), so a gold/XP change merged from another device also leaves the card stale.

title: Assistant Settings' 'Simple data requests' route is a dead control: nothing ever asks for the crud category, yet its 'Ollama · no model set' status shows on every Assistant page
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/settings-mac.png, memory-mac.png (footer); grep: the only uses of 'crud' are js/core/ai.js:35,44,87, js/core/aitools.js:3739 (a tool-ranking hint), js/modules/assistant.js:2136,2231; categories passed: assistant.js:686 and :1702 default 'complex'
rootCause: The four-category routing was designed before the single submission path settled on 'complex'; the setting outlived its caller.
fix: Either route the composer's short data requests to 'crud' (a real classifier) or remove the row and its footer status; default the route to Gemini rather than an Ollama route with no model.
detail: Settings › Model control offers four task routes. Every request in the app is sent as 'complex' (the composer, assistant.js:686, :1702), 'tutor' (topic actions, Help, PDF viewer, Creatives, Mind, Code review) or 'generation' (reports, reviews); no caller passes 'crud', so changing the Simple data requests provider, model or fallback has no effect. Its default (Ollama with an empty model) is what the sidebar footer prints as 'Ollama · local — no model set' on every Assistant page, which reads as a broken configuration on an iPad or iPhone where Ollama can never run.

title: Permissions offers 'Ask first' for read-only tools, but a read tool set to Ask first still runs without asking
evidence: eval: schedule_list tier 'read', options ['Default · runs freely','Ask first','Blocked']; js/modules/assistant.js:2517 (Ask first offered when tier !== consequential); js/core/aiorchestrator.js:147-155 (effectiveMode 'ask'), :726 (pause only for consequential or reversible+ask)
rootCause: The pause condition encodes tier rules instead of reading the effective mode.
fix: Pause whenever mode === 'ask' regardless of tier (keep the read tools' approval card short), or stop offering Ask first on read tools.
detail: Every non-consequential tool's select offers 'Ask first', including the read tier (e.g. Read schedule, Files list/text, Money overview). effectiveMode() returns 'ask' for it, but the executor only pauses for confirmation when the tool is consequential or (reversible AND mode ask), so a read tool the user tightened to Ask first runs silently. A user who wants to approve, say, files_list or money_transactions before Kurenai reads them gets no approval card.

title: Assistant chat header's Project picker and Pin are 21px-tall chips on iPad (touch targets far under 44px)

'done' is the raw status, '#1' an internal record id, and 'todo_add_task' the function name. title: No space between consecutive blocks in an Assistant reply (table runs straight into the code block)

rootCause: Rich blocks (.k-asst-table, .k-asst-codeblock) carry no block spacing
fix: Give the message body a flow gap (e.g. .k-asst-msg-body > * + * { margin-block-start: var(--sp-10) }) instead of per-element margins.

title: Morning Review text has a double full stop and lower-cases the warning's title ('revision block 24 is 7 days away..')
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/notif-seeded-mac.png (Morning review row: 'Exam season is on: revision block 24 is 7 days away.. A good first task'); js/core/dayreview.js:540; body built at js/core/exams.js:1078
rootCause: String concatenation assumes the warning body has no punctuation and no proper nouns.
fix: Strip a trailing full stop before appending and do not lower-case the body (lower-case only the first character if needed).
detail: The template appends ': ' + body.toLowerCase() + '.' to a warning body that already ends with a full stop, giving 'away..', and lower-cases proper nouns and codes inside it (an exam named 'AQA 7517 Paper 1' becomes 'aqa 7517 paper 1'). Visible in the notification feed and the review.

title: Permissions on iPhone: each area's disclosure chevron is pushed off-screen and the filter field floats unaligned
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/perm-iphone.png; eval at iphone: .k-asst-chev rect [414,385,6,20], parent row [38..364]; filter 200x32 vs Reset 44 tall; js/modules/assistant.js:2494, 2545-2553

title: Storage rounds small data to '0 KB' (a 5-byte file, 2 ink pages) while Pen and ink says '1 KB of ink'

title: Archive pages disagree on their kicker: 'The archive · 通' on Backup, Help and Notifications, 'Settings · 庫' on Storage, Pen and ink and Connections
evidence: shots/assistant-archive/notif-seeded-mac.png, data-seed-mac.png, help-seed-mac.png vs storage-seed-mac.png, pen-seed-mac.png, connections-seed-mac.png, storage-empty-ipad.png

title: A fresh install's first notification is backdated: '23 plan topics carried over into this week', dated Monday 08:00, before the app existed

detail: On an empty account opened on Friday 6 November, the feed already holds the Pacing carry-over notice timestamped Monday 2 November 08:00, telling a brand-new user they are behind on 23 rows of the seeded plan, plus a Morning Review about the SAMPLE mock exam. A first open greets the user with backlog they never had.

reviewNote: HOTFIXED 8 Nov (sw kos-malfix-1, 9fecf63, smoke114): the cause is stopped. Clean-up of the 1,741 phantom ledger entries, the phantom XP/gold, the badge tiers and the two journals waits for the user's decision in the plan.
title: Sync rewards never stop: bulkUpsert matches by MAL id across modules, so an anime sharing a manga's MAL id flips the manga row to anime and back every autosync cycle, paying a reward each time and flooding the 2,000-entry session ledger (UR-21, live: 1,741 entries)
devices: all (every device that runs autosync pays and evicts on its own)
evidence: docs/audit/2026-11/findings/live-account.md LA-31 (live counts); docs/audit/2026-11/harness/ur21-repro.js (jsdom + fake-indexeddb, real bulkUpsert/mirrorOpts/logSyncRewardBatch) and docs/audit/2026-11/data/ur21-repro-output.txt: each books pull pays [Death Note, statusAdvanced] in all 3 cycles; the One Piece row is never created (3 rows, not 4).
rootCause: Provider identity is not scoped by module in bulkUpsert (MAL ids are per type); the reward watermark (invariant 17) assumes one row is one media item and is absorbed even by a cross-module merge. Cf. HANDOFF §6.21 (rewards without idempotent receipts).
fix: (1) In tryAnilist/tryMal use index.getAll(value) and keep only rows whose module matches (no schema change; compound [module,id] indexes would need DB v9, invariant 6); merge() refuses old.module !== inc.module. (2) rewardDelta pays nothing when a merge changed module or provider identity; consider once per entry per day. (3) Regression smoke: two cycles with a colliding MAL id pay once, make 4 rows, leave the manga untouched. (4) One-time repair at boot: prune the bogus journal events; the anime insert on the next pull. (5) USER DECISION: delete the 1,741 bogus ledger entries (frees room, cannot restore evicted ones), claw back XP/gold or not (no clawback by default), and the badge tiers (invariant 162). Stopgap with no code: turn off Collection autosync until the fix ships.
detail: LIVE (8 Nov, the user's account, read-only, LA-31): 1,741 of the 2,000 ledger entries are sync-reward sessions naming Death Note and Aku no Kyouten (Books), about 40 a day since 27 Sep, each {xp 46, gold 12}: about 80,500 XP and 21,000 spendable gold of phantom pay. Real sessions are evicted by the cap (sessions.js:31 CAP=2000), so the ledger now reaches back only to about 27 Sep, which cuts streaks, a topic's minutes, goals over past ranges and Reports' longer totals. The cloud state has lost them too. MECHANISM: MAL numbers anime and manga separately, so MAL 21 is both the Death Note manga and One Piece (TV). AniList ids never collide. bulkUpsert's identity cascade (mediadb.js:1183-1213) looks up the GLOBAL 'anilist' and 'mal' indexes (:119, :126) with no module check (unlike cloudsync findByProviderId :886 and media.js dedupeVault :316). The anime pull (autosync.js:117-125) misses anilist 21, finds the manga row by mal 21, and merges One Piece (planned, 0, volumes null) into it. The reward watermark absorbs down (mediadb.js:1168). 2.5 s later the books pull misses anilist 30021 (the row now carries 21), finds the row by mal 21 again, and merges Death Note back. rewardDelta (:398-410, :1155) sees statusAdvanced (+36 units for Aku no Kyouten), and governor.js:284-295 pays 46 XP and 12 gold through logSyncRewardBatch (media.js:198). Journals gain volumes null→N every cycle (journalFacts :462-466, journalDiff :489-497); status pairs cancel within a day (:500-516). Collateral: those anime never get a row (the mirror is broken, invariant 90); kos_media is pushed twice a cycle and may upload the anime-shaped copy under the manga's syncId; gold/level badge tiers earned from the phantom pay are permanent (invariant 162); Reports' earned figures are inflated about 3,200 XP and 840 gold a week. gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
title: Todoist: a reminder made on one device is duplicated when another device syncs before the state document arrives
evidence: Re-run 7 Nov: exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']], remote ['T3']. Also reachable on ONE device through two tabs (see the lease finding). Original: exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']], remote: ['T3']; js/core/exttasks.js:180-187 (import with no matching attempt), js/core/ext.js:306-316 (syncProvider takes the lease without pulling the cloud state first), js/core/exttasks.js:229-237
rootCause: Remote link state is replicated asynchronously while the remote cursor (sync token) is per device; import has no identity check beyond byLink.
fix: Make the cycle state-consistent: before taking the lease run a cloud pull (KOS.cloudsync cycle) and push the state right after the cycle; and in reconcile's import path, before adding, look for an existing reminder already linked to that remote id (dedupe byLink after any merge) or an unlinked one in the same list whose uuidOf('add|'+uid) is pending (record pending adds {uid→temp} in state.ext so any device can recognise its own item_add). Also add a boot/merge pass that folds two reminders linked to the same ext.id.
detail: The lease serialises Todoist network work between devices, but the LINK (reminder.ext.id) lives in the synced state document, which reaches the other device later. Device A pushes a new reminder (item_add) and links it locally; device B takes the lease next (A releases it at once) while its state still holds the reminder unlinked and its own per-device sync token predates the add. B's incremental pull returns the new Todoist task, finds no local link (byLink) and reconcile() imports it as a SECOND reminder linked to the same Todoist id; the cloud merge then keeps both (different ids/uids). Reproduced in jsdom with the smoke112 fake: after the B-side cycle, two local reminders 'Made on A' are both linked to T3 while Todoist has one task.
