gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
title: Todoist: a failed second command batch leaves the first batch's tasks unlinked, so the next sync imports them as duplicates
evidence: Re-run 7 Nov: exp/td.js chunk → cycle1 false 'Todoist answered 503.', remote 45 / local linked 0; cycle2 local total 105, dup 45. Original: exp/td.js chunk → 'cycle1 false Todoist answered 503 / remote items 45 local linked 0 / cycle2: local total 105 dup local 45'; js/core/exttasks.js:318-335 (ok callbacks only after the reduce over chunks resolves), js/core/exttasks.js:241-243 (token saved only after push)
rootCause: Non-atomic multi-request push with all-or-nothing local bookkeeping.
fix: Apply each chunk's results as soon as it returns (run the after[] entries whose commands are all in that chunk's sync_status), keep an item's parent and sub-task adds in one chunk, and persist the link/temp-id map before the next request; on the pull side, treat an incoming task whose id appears in a stored temp_id_mapping as already linked.
detail: tdPush sends commands in chunks of 90 and runs every 'ok' callback (which writes the link and base) only after ALL chunks succeed. If chunk 2 fails (HTTP 429/5xx, offline, tab suspended), chunk 1's item_add commands have already created tasks in Todoist but nothing local is linked, and the sync token is not saved either. The next cycle pulls those tasks with the old token, finds no local link and imports each as a new reminder; the originals are then re-sent as item_add. Linking a list with ~45+ reminders that have a sub-task each exceeds 90 commands on the first cycle. Reproduced: 60 reminders with one sub each, chunk 2 answered 503 → cycle 2 leaves 105 local reminders (45 duplicates).

gverdict: confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov

title: Two open tabs or windows overwrite each other's saves (last writer wins on the whole state)
devices: mac (two windows/tabs), iPad Safari with two tabs
evidence: Re-checked 7 Nov: no 'storage' listener, BroadcastChannel or navigator.locks anywhere in js/ (grep); store.save still writes the whole document (store.js:395-410). Original: kos.mjs eval 17 (iframe experiment) → {afterBsaved:true, finalHasA:true, finalHasB:false, inMemA_hasB:false}; js/core/store.js:395-410 (whole-document save), no 'storage' listener anywhere in js/ (grep)

A change made in one tab is erased by the next save in the other. title: Todoist: a full sync drops completed sub-tasks from the reminder (and can re-add them to Todoist as duplicates)

rootCause: Absence in a full sync is interpreted as deletion.
fix: Do not reset the mirror on a full sync triggered by a link change; only drop entries of projects no longer linked. Treat a sub missing from a full sync as 'unknown', not deleted (keep subs whose remote child is not returned unless is_deleted arrives), and never re-add a sub that has an x.
detail: When the linked-project signature changes (linking or unlinking any list) the cycle requests sync_token '*' and resets the mirror. Todoist's full sync returns only active items, so completed sub-tasks are absent from the mirror; the parent's remote subs then differ from base and the pull overwrites the local subs, deleting every ticked sub-task. If the local subs were also edited, local wins, and each local sub whose x is no longer in the mirror is sent again as item_add, duplicating it in Todoist. Reproduced with a fake that, like Todoist, omits checked items from a full sync: 'Plan' (ticked) vanished locally after linking a second list. Depends on Todoist excluding completed sub-items from a full sync (documented behaviour for completed tasks).

title: Todoist: completing a repeating reminder here sends a new due string instead of closing the occurrence
evidence: Re-run 7 Nov: exp/td.js recur → cmds [[item_update {id:T1,due:{date:'2026-11-05',string:'every week',is_recurring:true}}]]; x-rule 'Gym' → [[item_close]]. Original: exp/td.js recur → cmds [[{type:item_update,args:{id:T1,due:{date:'2026-11-05',string:'every week',is_recurring:true}}}]]; gym: local done=true, cmds [[item_close]]; js/core/reminders.js:229-236, js/core/exttasks.js:99-107, 282-290
rootCause: Local recurrence semantics duplicated instead of delegated to the provider that owns the rule.
fix: For a linked repeating reminder, push item_close (Todoist rolls the date itself) and let the pull bring the new date back; treat ext.rs rules as repeating in complete() (roll forward with Todoist as the source) so both paths behave alike.
detail: KOS.reminders.complete() rolls a repeating reminder forward locally (new due, done=false) so the push sees only a 'when' change and sends item_update with due {date: next, string: 'every week', is_recurring}. Todoist never records the completion (no history/karma, completed view empty), and since Todoist parses due.string, the explicit date may be ignored and re-anchored to today, which the next pull brings back. For a Todoist-only rule (ext.rs, e.g. 'every mon, fri') the reminder instead closes locally (recur is null here) and sends item_close, so it shows as completed until the next pull un-completes it with Todoist's new date: two different behaviours for the same action.

title: A 404 on an update deletes the local event or reminder (e.g. after reconnecting a different Google account)

Clear (or archive) ext links on disconnect and on connecting a different account (compare the account id).

title: The whole state lives in one localStorage key with no fallback: when it outgrows the quota every later change is lost on reload
evidence: Re-measured 7 Nov: seeded 372,887 chars (srs 110,391; pacing 84,696; sessions 84,052), empty 96,139; tight quota fill → console 'save failed QuotaExceededError … kurenai-os-v1 exceeded the quota', the reminder not stored until space was freed and flush() ran. The curriculum alone has 5,436 flashcards, so a fully reviewed deck is ~0.9 MB before Code, Japanese facets and Mind cards, and every new domain adds to the same document. Chrome refused the write at ~5.2 M characters total; WebKit's limit is of the same order. When setItem throws, save() shows one toast ('Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.') and keeps running on the in-memory copy; every later change, and the pagehide flush (which only logs, store.js:417-425), is lost on the next reload or when iOS evicts the page. title: Every replicated store pulls with a strict updated_at > cursor on now() stamps, so a row committed late is skipped forever
evidence: Re-read 7 Nov: q.gt('updated_at', …) at cloudsync.js:358/376, money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324 and push.js:90; kos_touch_updated_at still sets now() (migration 20260716000001:26-35). Original: supabase/migrations/20260716000001_kos_sync_init.sql:26-35 (now()); q.gt('updated_at', …) at js/core/money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324, cloudsync.js:358/376; cursor = max seen (money.js:1189, 1207)
rootCause: Timestamp cursor over transaction-start timestamps.
fix: Stamp with clock_timestamp() in the trigger and pull with an overlap window (gt cursor − 2 minutes) — every store already skips its own echo by stamp or uid, so re-reading a few rows is harmless; or use a monotonic bigserial 'version' column per table as the cursor.
detail: Media, files, money, reviews, mind, ink, reports and push all pull 'updated_at > cursor' and then advance the cursor to the largest updated_at seen. The touch trigger stamps updated_at := now(), which in Postgres is the TRANSACTION START time. If device A's upsert (a 500-row media chunk, a money batch) starts at t1 and commits after device B's quicker write stamped t2 > t1, a third device that pulls between the two commits sets its cursor to t2 and never fetches A's rows (t1 < t2). Nothing ever re-reads them: the pulling device silently lacks those transactions/reviews/ink strokes until a restore. With three devices syncing on focus this is a real, if rare, divergence with no symptom.

title: Todoist: moving a task to another linked project in Todoist is undone by the next sync
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td2.js moveRemote → 'after remote move local: [{list:1 (School), ext:{id:T1,list:P1}}] cmds [[item_move:{id:T1,project_id:P1}]] remote project P1'; js/core/exttasks.js:191-196 (reconcile writes ext.list only, never listId), 270 (moved = lk.id !== it.ext.list), 287 (item_move to the local list's project)
rootCause: The list is not a three-way-merged field: the pull records the remote project in ext.list, and the push reads any difference between ext.list and the local list as a LOCAL move.
fix: In reconcile, when remote.list differs from base list and maps to another linked Reminders list, move the reminder there (listId = linked[remote.list]) inside inbound; only treat a local listId change (lk.id !== base list) as a local move. Keep a base list in ext.base so the three-way rule applies to the list as to every other field.
detail: Two Reminders lists are linked to two Todoist projects (School→P1, Home→P2). Move a synced task from School to Home in Todoist. The next cycle does not move the reminder (its listId stays School; only ext.list becomes P2), and tdPush then sees ext.list (P2) differ from the local list's project (P1) and sends item_move back to P1. title: A linked reminder moved to a list linked to the other provider is copied there and orphaned in the first
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td2.js moveLocal → 'moved to unlinked: cmds []', 'edit while unlinked: cmds [[item_update:{id:T1,content:Local move edited}]]', 'remote rename reaches unlinked list item: Remote rename list 3'; js/core/exttasks.js:412 (!linkedHere → gtCreate, ext replaced at 437-440), 254-258 (Todoist add only when not linked; nothing queues a delete when the list link changes), 270 (moved only when the new list is a todoist link)

fix: Treat a list change as a change of link: when a reminder's list link provider/project differs from ext.p/ext.list, queue a delete (or item_move for same provider) for the old link in state.ext.deletes and clear ext before the other provider creates. For an unlinked target list, either queue the remote delete or unlink (ask once).

Move a Todoist-linked reminder to a list linked to Google Tasks (or the reverse): gtPush sees ext.p !== 'gtasks' and creates a Google task, overwriting ext with the Google link; the Todoist task is neither deleted nor unlinked. The Todoist mirror still holds it, so the next time it changes in Todoist (or on a full sync) byLink('todoist') finds no reminder and imports it again as a NEW reminder: one item becomes two, in two services. Moving a linked reminder to an UNLINKED list keeps it linked and both-way syncing (verified: a title edit is still pushed, a Todoist rename still lands on the reminder in the unlinked list), which contradicts 'a list links to ONE project' (invariant 160).

title: Creatives' file store is shared by the real account and the Empty and Sample review namespaces

title: The Todoist/Google sync lease does not exclude a second tab on the same device, and is never renewed during a long cycle
evidence: js/core/ext.js:73-77 (device() = state.ui.extDevice, shared by every tab of the profile), 268-270 (lease once per cycle, LEASE_S 120 at :40), 306-319 (no renewal); supabase/migrations/20261030000001_kos_ext.sql:44 (lease_holder = p_holder re-grants); in-tab guard only: js/core/ext.js:326 (var running); duplicate end state reproduced by audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']]
rootCause: Exclusion is designed per device, but the app's real unit of concurrency is the tab.
fix: Make the holder per tab (device id + a random per-page suffix kept in memory) or coordinate tabs with a Web Lock (navigator.locks.request('kos-ext-'+p)) / BroadcastChannel; renew the lease between chunks and lists, and abort the cycle when renewal fails. Also de-duplicate on pull: before importing an unknown remote id, look for a local reminder already linked to it.
detail: The lease holder is state.ui.extDevice, one id per browser profile, and kos_ext_lease grants the lease to the holder that already has it. Two open tabs or windows (or the Home Screen app plus a Safari tab on the iPad) therefore both 'win' and run their cycles at the same time against the same media-kv mirror and sync token. Each tab holds its own in-memory reminders (the two-tab clobber finding), so tab B's pull meets the task tab A just created and linked as an unknown remote item and imports it as a new reminder, while B's own unlinked copy is item_add'ed with the same uuid and linked to the same Todoist id: two reminders, one task — the same end state as the two-device duplicate, reachable on ONE device. Separately, the lease is 120 s and is never extended; a cycle that runs longer (several 90-command chunks, a slow network, Google Tasks paging) lets another device in mid-cycle.

title: Money, the review log, Mind's Journal and saved Reports replicate with no error surfaced anywhere
evidence: callers without cb: js/core/money.js:1220, 1226-1227; js/core/reviewlog.js:212; js/core/mindjournal.js:260, 267-268; js/core/reportstore.js:417, 423; contrast js/modules/inkset.js:92 (ink shows its result); js/core/money.js:1193-1206 (deleteRaw/putRaw callbacks take no err, meta.cursor = maxTs); js/modules/cloudui.js:86, 190 ('Last synced' from cloudsync status only)
rootCause: Each replicator copied Money's pattern, which treats replication as fire-and-forget; there is no shared status contract for secondary stores.
fix: Give every replicator a status record (last ok, last error, pending count) in a shared registry (e.g. KOS.cloudsync.sideStatus(name, …)) and render it in Archive › Cloud sync as one line per store; only advance a cursor after the local write succeeded.
detail: Each side store's syncCloud(cb) is only ever called WITHOUT a callback (debounced after a change, at boot and on a 30-minute interval), so an RLS refusal, a missing table, a network error or a failed chunk is dropped: nothing is logged, nothing is shown, and Archive › Cloud sync's 'Last synced' describes the state document only. A user who adds transactions on the iPhone can see 'Last synced 10:42' on both devices while kos_money has rejected every upsert. Only handwriting has a visible status (Pen and ink). The local put/delete callbacks in the pull ignore their error argument too, and the cursor is still advanced (money.js:1205-1206), so a row that failed to write locally is skipped for good.

title: 'Reset everything' only resets the state document: the media vault, files, money, ink, Mind, reviews, Creatives and reports all stay

title: Todoist: a command the server rejects is resent on every cycle forever, with no status shown
evidence: Re-read 7 Nov: exttasks.js:329-334 unchanged (only all-ok entries call a.ok; non-ok sync_status ignored). Original: js/core/exttasks.js:329-334 (only the all-ok case is handled; errors in r.sync_status are dropped), js/core/exttasks.js:256 (delete queue entry kept on error)
rootCause: Error results of batched commands are ignored.
fix: Read sync_status errors: for 'not found' (error_code 22) drop the queue entry or unlink the record; for other errors record them in counts and setStatus so Connections shows 'n changes refused' with the reason; apply per-command bookkeeping rather than per group.
detail: tdPush applies a record's bookkeeping only when every command in its group returns 'ok'. A rejected command (item_update or item_delete for a task deleted or moved out of reach in Todoist, an invalid label, a due string Todoist cannot parse) leaves base and the delete queue unchanged, so the same command is sent every cycle (every few minutes and on every focus) and the Connections status still says the cycle succeeded, because sync_status errors are never turned into counts or an error. A partly-applied group (item_update ok, item_close rejected) also re-sends the parts that did apply.

evidence: css/base.css:156-160 (rule inside @layer base); css/tokens.css:35 (@layer tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes); overriding rules e.g. css/components.css:406 .k-input, :417 .k-pill-select font-size var(--fs-12-5), css/views/assistant.css:216 .k-asst-input font-size var(--fs-14-5); measurement audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-iphone.jsonl (font16 lists per view, script a11y-scan.js) | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-measured at 402x874 on kos-redraw-1 (a11y21-iphone.jsonl): Assistant composer 14.5px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Files search 13.5px, Shrine/Wishlist status selects 12.5px, Seasonal year select 12.5px; the new picture drawer's condition selects are .k-input--sm too (js/modules/artslot.js:69). css/base.css:156-160 still sits in @layer base.
rootCause: Cascade-layer order: a base-layer guard cannot override component-layer declarations.
fix: Move the phone 16px rule to the last layer (themes, or an unlayered rule at the end of components.css) so it wins: @media (max-width:700px){ input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range]), select, textarea, [contenteditable] { font-size: max(16px, 1em) !important } } — or set --fs-input tokens that components read. Add a smoke check that no visible field computes under 16px at 402px.
detail: Invariant 40 promises 16px inputs on the phone, and base.css sets input, select, textarea { font-size: max(16px, 1em) } under max-width 700px. That rule lives in @layer base, which the declared order (tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes) puts BELOW every component and view rule, so any class that sets a font size wins. Measured at 402x874: Assistant composer 14.5px, Reminders quick-add 14px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Help search 13px, Files search 13.5px, Backup & Restore e-mail/password 13.5px, Routines settings times 13.5px, Media Sync inputs 13.5px, Assignments subtask input 13px, every .k-pill-select sort/filter (Assignments, Exams & Papers, Shrine, Wishlist, topic page reader select, Card stats retention) 12.5px, Pacing lesson-day selects 12px, vault score corners 14px. On the user's iPhone each of these zooms the viewport when tapped and leaves it zoomed (the layout then scrolls sideways until pinched back). Only the phone search sheet was special-cased (layout.css:457).

title: Undo in toasts cannot be reached by keyboard or screen reader
evidence: js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex '-1' at :76, 8000 ms timer :81, announce(msg) without the action); index.html:140 (#toast aria-hidden=true); callers js/modules/dayreview.js:534,615,621,622, js/modules/reminders.js:344 | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-read js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex -1, 8000 ms, announce(msg) only) and index.html:141 (#toast aria-hidden=true).
rootCause: #toast was made purely visual in Phase F; the later action variant reused it without restoring access.
fix: Give action toasts a focusable, named Undo: drop tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden on the action toast (or render action toasts in a non-hidden region), announce 'msg. Undo available (Ctrl/Cmd+Z)', pause the timer on hover/focus, and add a global Cmd/Ctrl+Z that runs the latest toast action.
detail: The one Undo route for Daily Review triage (Tomorrow, Done, Study block) and Reminders' 'ticked in your plan' is a button inside #toast. #toast is aria-hidden="true" and the button is created with tabindex=-1, so it is out of the tab order and hidden from assistive tech; the announced sentence ('<title> · moved to tomorrow') never mentions Undo. The toast disappears after 8 s with no pause on hover/focus (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.2.1 Timing). A keyboard or VoiceOver user has no undo for these actions.

title: Focus chime is silent on iPhone/iPad and has no on/off or volume setting
evidence: js/modules/focus.js:788-801 (chime(): new AC() on first call from tick, no ctx.resume()); call sites :496, :508, :522 inside the interval tick; grep -rniE '"(Sound|Chime)' js/modules js/core → none | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): js/modules/focus.js:788-800 unchanged: AudioContext created lazily at chime time with no unlock on a gesture and no setting.
rootCause: Audio unlock rules of iOS WebKit not handled; no audio preference model.
fix: Create/resume the AudioContext in Start's click handler (unlock it), call ctx.resume() before each chime, and add a Focus setting 'Sound at cycle end' (on/off + volume, per device in state.ui). Also send a device notification for cycle end when the page is hidden.
detail: The only sound in the app (Pomodoro cycle end, break end, stopwatch break nudge) is a Web Audio oscillator whose AudioContext is created lazily inside the timer tick, never from a user gesture and never resume()d. WebKit starts such a context 'suspended', so on the user's iPhone and iPad the chime never plays; the cue is then only a 2.6 s toast that a user away from the screen will miss. There is also no setting anywhere to turn the chime off, choose a sound or set its volume (grep finds no Sound/Chime control). Japanese voice lines and the Assistant's speech are the only other audio.

title: Status chips fail AA contrast app-wide (3.5–4.3:1 at 11.5px), worst in Atelier Dawn
evidence: css/components.css:191-199 (.k-chip: color var(--chip-c); background color-mix(var(--chip-c) 18%, transparent)); scan output audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-mac-dawn2.jsonl and a11y-mac.jsonl (script audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-scan.js); token ratios computed: Dawn --red on --s1 5.78, on its own wash 3.68 | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Graphite, seeded, this build: k-chip 'Free' (Gold Shop) 3.94, '○ Not enough evidence' 3.94, goal.pace '◌ Too early to call' 3.94, 'In progress' 4.35, 'Gemini · auto' 4.28, '◆ Priority purchase' 4.23 (all 11.5px); Dawn Home day dot '5' 3.42 @14px.

title: Touch-size floor is undone by shared primitives: pill selects 30px, switches 34x20, checkboxes 18x18 on iPad and iPhone
evidence: css/base.css:115-121 (:where(...) floor; no input[type=checkbox], no .k-switch); css/components.css:417 (.k-pill-select { min-block-size: 0 } cancels it); css/components.css:207 (.k-switch fixed --fx-switch-w/h, not in the coarse block at :669-677); css/layout.css:233-235 (.k-rail-toggle at --hit-dense); measurements audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-ipad.jsonl, a11y-iphone.jsonl | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Under touch at 820x1180 and 402x874: switches still 34x20 on the new Avatar & profile page (gov.theme-follow, gov.art-on, gov.art-reduced), the Wall's List view, Focus penalty, Pen and ink, Exams; Seasonal year select 96x31; the Assistant's Pin/Hide/Voice chips 21px tall (see the Assistant finding).

fix: Drop the bare Backspace binding (keep Alt+←/→ and the buttons), or at least ignore it when a [role=dialog][aria-modal=true], the Focus overlay, a review sheet or the Exam Room is open and when focus is inside #main controls.

title: The Wall, the Seat's showcase and Edit your seat wait 7-12 s on a dense account because every open re-measures all 254 badges
evidence: eval timings: list() 7867/920/7452 ms; per set: collection 5127, exams 1473, mind 1158, study 983, ALL 6954 ms; Wall body ready 12512 ms; Seat note after 12867 ms; js/core/achievements.js:329-341 (list → measureOne per DEF each call); shots/a11y-hci/t-wall-iphone.png ('Reading your records…'), t-seat-ipad.png (empty arc)

title: No dialog closes on navigation: the router leaves every open dialog, drawer and sheet over the next page
evidence: shots/a11y-hci/n-asst-ipadl.png (Home's hero drawer over the Assistant at 1180x820); eval: .k-dialog-overlay count 1, data-scroll-lock present after 7 hash changes; js/core/ui.js:155-240 (openDialog/dialogStack, no navigation hook); js/core/router.js (no dialog handling)
rootCause: Dialog lifetime is not tied to the route; each surface assumed the user leaves only via its own buttons.
fix: In the router's navigation path (before rendering a different view, not on KOS.rerender), close every dialog on the stack via its own close path (teardown runs onClose), or let a dialog opt in to staying ({keepOnNav}).

Reproduced: opened the picture drawer on Home (KOS.artSlot.open), then changed location.hash through #/files, #/reminders, #/calendar, #/goals, #/help and #/assistant: the Home hero drawer was still open over the Assistant (one .k-dialog-overlay, data-scroll-lock set). title: Assistant: Hide / Show Kurenai and Voice redraw the whole page and drop focus; the chips are 21px tall on the iPad
evidence: eval at 1180x820 touch: chips [[◇ Pin,45,21],[Hide,42,21],[Voice off,66,21]]; activeElement BODY after Hide/Show; js/modules/assistant.js:2039-2061 (setHidden -> KOS.show; Voice text + aria-pressed)
rootCause: Full-view redraw for a local toggle; chip class not covered by the touch floor.
fix: Toggle the presence panel in place (data-state) or restore focus to the counterpart chip after the redraw; give Voice a fixed label ("Voice") with aria-pressed; raise .k-asst-chip-btn to the touch minimum under pointer:coarse.
detail: Hide, Show Kurenai and the Voice chip each call KOS.show("assistant", ...) to redraw, so keyboard focus falls to <body> (measured activeElement BODY after Hide and after Show) and the user must tab back from the top. The Voice chip names its state in its label AND in aria-pressed, so VoiceOver reads "Voice off, toggle button, not pressed" (a double negative). On the iPad in landscape (touch) the Pin, Hide and Voice chips are 45x21, 42x21 and 66x21 px, under the 44px floor.

title: iPhone: Edit your seat's preview is the desktop Stage shrunk to 28% (4.5px text)
evidence: shots/a11y-hci/n-edit-empty-iphone.png; eval at 402x874: .k-gv-prev-inner transform matrix(0.278614…), smallest text box 4.46px; css/views/governor.css:150-151; js/modules/governor-ui.js:655-673
rootCause: The preview is a scaled desktop render regardless of the device.
fix: Under 700px preview the phone composition at 1:1 (or only the parts being edited: banner, title, sigil, showcase tray), and keep Save disabled until something changes.
detail: Edit your seat draws a live preview by rendering the 1328px-wide Stage and scaling it (transform: scale(var(--prev-s))). At 402px the scale is 0.279, so the preview's text is 4.5px tall and its showcase slots are dots; the preview is a picture of a page you cannot read, and it is not how the Seat looks on the phone (the phone Seat is a single column). The Save button is also shown as the primary action on first open with nothing changed (empty account).
